**1. Forward Bias Operation:**
- The positive terminal of the external battery is connected to the P-type region and the negative terminal to the N-type region.
- This opposes the built-in potential barrier, narrows the depletion region, and allows a large majority charge carrier current to flow easily once the barrier potential ($0.7\text{ V}$ for $	ext{Si}$, $0.3\text{ V}$ for $	ext{Ge}$) is crossed.

**2. Reverse Bias Operation:**
- The positive terminal is connected to the N-type region and the negative terminal to the P-type region.
- This reinforces the potential barrier, widens the depletion region, and blocks majority carriers. Only a very small reverse saturation current flows due to minority carriers.

**V-I Characteristics:**
```text
  I (mA)
    ^         Forward Bias
    |           /
    |          /
    |         /
----+--------+--------> V
    |      . |
    |    .   |
    |  .     | Reverse Breakdown
    v        v (V_z)
  Reverse Bias
```
proTip: Clearly label the knee voltage and reverse breakdown region in your V-I characteristic sketch.
